surprises.description: Centene reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $0.58, far above the preview’s roughly $0.07–$0.10 consensus range. The preview noted that the estimate was unusually low, but the reported beat was still much larger than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Centene reported Q3 2026 adjusted diluted EPS of $0.58, beating expectations, driven primarily by Medicare segment outperformance.”

surprises.description: Centene raised its 2026 adjusted EPS floor to greater than $5.20, above the prior greater-than-$4.80 guide and at the high end of the preview’s desired raise range. The preview expected a raise, but this was stronger than its base-case threshold of greater than $5.00.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance to greater than $5.20, up from prior guidance of greater than $4.80.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything short of a raise to the ‘>$5.00–$5.25’ zone will be read as management pre-funding a weak Q4 or a weak 2027.”

surprises.description: The 2027 adjusted EPS jump-off point is about $4.70 after removing $0.50 of non-recurring 2026 earnings, below the preview’s roughly $5.30 2027 consensus. However, management said it expects to grow EPS above both that baseline and the revised $5.20 2026 guidance, giving a more bullish growth commitment than a low baseline alone would suggest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided to an approximately $4.70 adjusted EPS jump-off point for 2027, stripping out $0.50 of non-recurring 2026 earnings ($180 million marketplace, $160 million Medicare), but expects to grow EPS above both the $4.70 baseline and the revised $5.20 guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 adj. EPS consensus | ~$5.30” and “Management must bridge over ~$0.50 of non-recurring 2026 items, Medicaid attrition, and the Stars hit.”

surprises.description: Centene said Medicare Advantage is on track to break even in 2026, a full year ahead of the preview’s expectation of breakeven-or-better in 2027. That is an earlier turnaround than investors were led to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Medicare Advantage is now on track to reach breakeven in 2026, a full year ahead of the turnaround plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Centene … has cut ~3,000 plans and exited 344 counties targeting MA breakeven-or-better in 2027.”

surprises.description: The PDP 2026 pretax margin outlook moved up to the mid-to-high 3% range from guidance of greater than 3%. The preview expected a margin above 3%, but did not anticipate this higher range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The PDP business raised its 2026 pretax margin outlook to the mid-to-high 3% range, up from the prior greater than 3% guidance.”

surprises.description: Although the preview expected Marketplace to remain within its 4.5%–5.0% margin target, Centene now expects a full-year result at the top of the range. This is a modestly better outcome than simply tracking within the range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marketplace is now expected to deliver a full-year pretax margin at the top of the 4.5% to 5% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Marketplace margin and morbidity. The 4.5–5.0% margin guide was Q2's biggest upside surprise.”

surprises.description: Centene disclosed $480 million in workforce and enterprise optimization costs, including $276 million of Q3 severance, which the preview did not anticipate. The company said the actions position SG&A as a tailwind for 2027, but the excluded-from-adjusted-results charges are a new near-term cost.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company recorded $480 million in workforce and enterprise optimization costs (excluded from adjusted results), including $276 million of severance in Q3, positioning SG&A as a tailwind for 2027.”

surprises.description: Centene plans to exit its roughly $4 billion Health Net commercial group business, a material portfolio change not flagged in the preview. The exit is to occur over 18 to 24 months, but the call facts provide no quantified earnings effect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Centene is exiting its roughly $4 billion Health Net commercial group business (largely in California) over the next 18 to 24 months.”

surprises.description: The call introduced specific 2027 headwinds from OB3 Medicaid attrition and removal of California’s unsatisfactory-immigration-status population. The preview discussed Medicaid work requirements and ACA subsidy risks, but did not identify these specific sources of additional attrition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[Centene] faces 2027 headwinds from OB3 Medicaid attrition and removal of the California unsatisfactory immigration status population.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Three structural 2027 headwinds — Medicaid work requirements starting in January, the post-subsidy ACA risk pool, and a severe Star Ratings downgrade now under litigation — all land in the same guide.”

surprises.description: Centene expects PDP margins to reset to 2%–3% in 2027, below the greater-than-3% margin level highlighted in the preview. This signals a weaker forward margin outlook even as the 2026 PDP outlook improved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PDP margins [are] expected to reset to a 2% to 3% range.”

surprises.description: Centene reported an additional $1.1 billion of senior-note repurchases since the Q2 call, alongside a lower 2026 interest-expense midpoint of $610 million. The preview anticipated further debt paydown but did not suggest a reduction of this size since Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total debt was reduced to $15.0 billion from $18.5 billion at the end of 2024, including an additional $1.1 billion of senior notes repurchased since the Q2 call, lowering interest expense to a $610 million midpoint for 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Secondary: capital deployment — buyback pace at ~$33.5B market cap, further debt paydown after Q1's $1.0B.”
